use_cases.description: An assistant that, for a given forklift, pulls its maintenance history, manual service intervals, and parts inventory, then proposes a preventive maintenance schedule that fits around warehouse shift and peak-load windows and flags parts that are out of stock before the service is due.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the scheduling conflicts with warehouse operations and part-availability delays by combining maintenance logs, manuals, and inventory into one view that planners can act on. The physical inspection and repair remain with technicians, so the assistant only reduces planning effort per job.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Fewer missed or late services and fewer parts-driven delays, but the physical work quality is unchanged.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports uptime and cost control in warehouse operations, a sensible but not top-line priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Maintenance logs and inventory are likely structured, but manual service intervals and log completeness are uncertain.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Retrieval over logs, manuals, and inventory with a scheduling rule layer; moderate integration with the inventory system.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Planners keep final say, so the workflow change is modest.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Enterprise CMMS tools offer scheduling and parts alerts, but adding manual-based reasoning usually needs customisation.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Equipment scheduling with no profiling of people is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Equipment and parts data contain no personal data, unless technician names are logged.

use_cases.description: A tool that reads free-text technician notes and inspection checklists from maintenance logs and converts them into structured fault codes, parts used, and time spent, so that recurring faults and parts consumption can be tracked.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the difficulty of acting on physical inspection outcomes by turning unstructured notes into structured records. This makes parts forecasting and recurring-fault tracking possible without changing the hands-on work itself.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Improves consistency of records, but only if technicians keep notes reasonably complete.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Helps maintenance and parts planning, a secondary operational benefit.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Free-text notes are unstructured and of uneven quality, which limits reliability.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Standard information extraction on text, with a mapping to a fixed fault taxonomy.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Technicians must still write notes, so the change is small but needs discipline.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Document extraction tools exist, but mapping to this fault taxonomy needs configuration.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Processing maintenance records with no profiling of people is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Technician names may appear in notes, which is indirect personal data.

process: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: An assistant that helps managers turn their rough notes and prior review scores into a consistently structured, neutral-toned draft performance review, which the manager then edits and owns.
use_cases.justification: Directly addresses the widely varying quality and tone of manager write-ups by giving every manager the same structure and tone guidance, while the manager remains the author who validates and edits the final text.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Improves consistency of structure and tone, though drafts still depend on the manager's input quality.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports fair and consistent talent processes, a moderate rather than top-line priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Manager narratives are free text and uneven, though scores are structured.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Off-the-shelf LLM drafting with a template and prompt guardrails; low build effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Managers must change how they write reviews and may distrust AI-drafted text.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: General-purpose writing assistants can be configured for this with light setup.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Drafting evaluations of employee performance falls under Annex III employment/worker evaluation, so it is high risk and needs strict human oversight and conformity controls.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Performance evaluations and personal file data are sensitive personal data requiring confidentiality controls.

use_cases.process_name: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: A tool that pre-screens draft reviews and prior scores to flag inconsistencies in rating language versus scores (e.g. a 'exceeds' score with weak narrative) and surfaces outliers for HR calibration, so the calibration meeting focuses on the cases that need discussion.
use_cases.justification: Targets the time-consuming calibration preparation by highlighting only the reviews whose narrative and scores diverge or sit far from peer norms, instead of HR reading every review.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Surfaces rating inconsistencies that reviewers might miss, but flags can be noisy.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports fairness and calibration quality, a moderate priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Scores are structured but calibration notes and narratives are inconsistent.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Needs integration with the review system and a tuned consistency rule set.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR and managers adjust to a new pre-meeting step, a modest change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Requires a custom build tied to the company's rating scales and HR system.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Classifying and ranking employees' performance evaluations is an Annex III worker-evaluation use, so high risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes individual performance scores and personal file data, which is sensitive.

use_cases.process_name: Annual performance review drafting and calibration

use_cases.description: An AI tool that reads current policy documents and broker quotes and extracts coverage terms, limits, deductibles, exclusions and premiums into a standardised comparison table, so quotes from different brokers can be compared side by side.
use_cases.justification: This targets the manual quote comparison pain point. Comparing terms across brokers is largely a transcription and alignment task on documents with inconsistent layouts, which extraction handles well. Reviewers still make the decision and check the extracted figures against source documents.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistent field extraction reduces transcription slips, but errors in extracted terms must still be checked by a person.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports cost control through better quote comparison, but insurance is a modest spend line.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Broker quotes come in varied formats and PDFs, so extraction quality will vary by broker.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Standard document extraction into a fixed schema; moderate tuning per broker format.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Procurement keeps the same decision process, with a new comparison view added.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document extraction tools exist, though the schema will need configuring.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal procurement of insurance with no profiling of people is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Policy and quote documents are business records, with at most indirect personal data.

use_cases.description: A Q&A assistant that lets Finance and Procurement ask questions about the current policy and draft renewal terms (for example, what changed, what is excluded, which claims affected cover) and returns answers with citations to the source clauses and claims history, for a human to review.
use_cases.justification: This addresses the complex policy terms pain point, where staff lack insurance expertise in-house. The assistant retrieves and summarises clauses for a human to interpret; it does not give legal advice or make renewal decisions, so the expert review stays in place.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Speeds up clause lookup and reduces missed clauses, but answers can be wrong and need expert checking.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Helps risk and compliance understanding of cover, an indirect priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Policy documents are available but may be scattered across files and versions.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Retrieval over a bounded document set with citations; a standard pattern.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Optional tool for staff; the working process does not change much.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Enterprise document Q&A tools are widely available.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal tool for staff with no profiling; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Claims history may contain indirect personal data about insured people or sites.

use_cases.description: A customer-facing chat assistant that answers return-eligibility questions from the return policy rules and the customer's order history, and drafts a recommended authorization decision for the live agent to confirm.
use_cases.justification: Targets the high volume of repetitive return-eligibility questions by answering routine cases directly and reducing agent handling time; agents stay in control of the final decision.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistent policy answers for routine questions, but edge cases still need human judgement.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports customer service cost control and throughput, a secondary priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Policy rules and order history are structured and largely available.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires integration with order system and policy knowledge base, moderate effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents shift from answering questions to reviewing AI drafts, a moderate workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature customer-service chat platforms support this with policy grounding.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Customer-facing chatbot, so limited-risk transparency obligations apply; no profiling of employees.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses order history linked to individual customers, which is indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: A tool that automatically pulls purchase date, order status, and product condition evidence (including uploaded photos) from order and return systems into a single structured summary for the agent to review.
use_cases.justification: Addresses agents having to check multiple systems to verify purchase date and condition, cutting lookup time and making the eligibility check more complete.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces missed checks across systems, though photo condition assessment is less reliable.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports handling-time and cost goals in customer service.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Order data is structured, but condition photos and system records are inconsistently captured.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Needs integration across several systems, a custom build.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Agents keep the same decision step, with less manual lookup.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Requires custom integration to the company's order and returns systems.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Internal back-office data consolidation with no profiling of people, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Consolidates customer order and photo data, indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: An automated matching engine that pairs bank statement lines with general ledger transactions using amount, date window, reference and counterparty rules plus learned patterns from prior reconciliations, and labels each item as auto-matched, probable match needing review, or unmatched.
use_cases.justification: The core pain point is manually matching thousands of transactions against bank statements under deadline pressure. Automating the high-confidence matches removes most of the manual matching effort, and leaves analysts to focus on the exceptions that actually need tracing.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Rule-based matching is more consistent than manual matching across thousands of lines, though edge cases still need review.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports the close deadline and cost control priorities of finance.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Bank and GL data are structured, but reference fields and prior workpapers may be inconsistent.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Reconciliation matching is a mature pattern requiring integration with the ERP and bank feeds.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Controllers keep final sign-off, so the change is moderate and familiar.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several mature bank reconciliation and finance automation tools exist.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Matches transactions, with no profiling of people or regulated use.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Contains payment and counterparty data that is business-related and only indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: An assistant that, for each unmatched or discrepant item, retrieves the related source documents, prior-period treatment and the likely cause of the difference, and presents a traced explanation to the accountant for review and decision.
use_cases.justification: The zero-tolerance requirement means every discrepancy must be traced to the exact transaction. This tool speeds up the investigation of exceptions without making any posting decisions, which keeps the accountant in control.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Improves traceability of exceptions, but the accountant still has to verify every explanation.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports close timeliness and control quality in finance.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Depends on linking bank lines to source documents, which is only partly consistent today.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Retrieval over ledger and workpapers with a language layer, moderate build effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Accountants investigate the same items with better context, so the workflow change is small.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Requires customization to the company's ledger and workpaper structure.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Supports finance investigation with no profiling of people.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Mostly business transaction data, with limited personal counterparty details.

use_cases.description: An assistant that takes approved content from the content calendar and prepares platform-specific versions (character limits, hashtags, asset sizes per platform guidelines) ready to load into each platform's scheduler, with a human confirming each post before it goes live.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the manual copying of approved content into each platform's scheduler by generating platform-ready drafts from the single approved source, reducing repetitive re-keying. A marketer still reviews and schedules each post.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces copy-paste errors and enforces platform formatting rules consistently across channels.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports marketing efficiency but is a secondary, not top-line, priority for an industrial distributor.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approved content and platform guidelines are structured and readily available in the calendar and asset library.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Text reformatting against stated platform rules is a well-established generation pattern with light integration.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Marketers still review and schedule, so the workflow change is modest.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several social scheduling suites already offer per-platform adaptation of content.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Marketing content generation with no profiling of people is minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Only company content and brand assets are processed, with no personal data.

use_cases.description: A workflow agent that tracks approval status across stakeholders, sends reminders to pending approvers, and maintains a single status view of each post (draft, pending approval, approved, scheduled, published), escalating overdue items to the marketing lead. It does not publish content without a human sign-off.
use_cases.justification: Addresses coordinating approval across multiple stakeholders and tracking pending versus published posts. Chasing approvers and reconciling statuses across tools is multi-step, cross-system work that a simple assistant cannot do on its own.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Fewer missed approvals and stale posts, though gains depend on stakeholder responsiveness.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Improves campaign throughput, a supporting rather than top priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Approval sign-offs and status data may be spread across email and tools, so consistency varies.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires integration with approval channels and scheduler status, a moderate build.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Stakeholders must work through the tracked approval flow, which may meet some resistance.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Work-management tools offer approval workflows, but a cross-tool status agent needs custom configuration.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Tracks content approvals, not individual performance, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Stakeholder names and approval records are indirectly personal data.

use_cases.description: A classifier that reads each new ticket's description and metadata and assigns a consistent severity level at submission, so severity no longer depends on how the requester happened to word or rate the issue.
use_cases.justification: Addresses tickets being inconsistently categorized by severity on submission, which forces engineers to re-triage manually. Consistent severity at intake also feeds the routing step.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Gives a consistent severity baseline where today it varies by requester, a clear consistency gain.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports operational efficiency and SLA adherence, a secondary rather than top-line priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Ticket descriptions are free text and sometimes sparse, so label quality depends on history being usable.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Standard text classification on ticket fields with a fixed severity scheme.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Requesters see a suggested severity; the workflow change is small.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: ITSM suites (e.g. ServiceNow, Jira Service Management) ship with classification and triage features.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Classifies tickets, not people; no profiling of employees, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Ticket text may contain requester names and contact details, so personal data is indirectly involved.

use_cases.description: A routing model that suggests the owning team or on-call engineer for each new ticket, based on ticket content, past resolved incidents, and the current on-call rotation, with a human dispatcher confirming the assignment.
use_cases.justification: Targets engineers spending time working out who should own a ticket. Routing from historical resolution patterns and the rotation schedule removes most of that lookup effort.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Routes tickets using resolution history, which should reduce misrouting and bounce-backs compared with ad hoc triage.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly reduces mean time to resolve and on-call load, a useful operational priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Incident history is structured and available, but ownership tags may be inconsistent in older records.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Needs integration with the ticketing system and rotation schedule, moderate effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Engineers and dispatchers keep final say, so the change is modest.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Major ITSM platforms offer assignment rules and some ML routing; full fit may need configuration.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Routes incidents to teams; it assigns work based on ticket content, not on individual behaviour or performance, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Rotation schedule and assignee names are personal data, indirectly processed.

use_cases.description: A duplicate-detection model that compares each new ticket against open and recent tickets and system logs, flagging likely duplicates of an existing incident for linking or merging.
use_cases.justification: Addresses duplicate tickets for the same incident not being detected, which inflates queue volume and wastes engineer time on the same problem twice.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Catches duplicates that humans miss across many similar tickets, though near-duplicates with different wording remain hard.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Reduces queue noise and wasted effort, a modest operational gain.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Ticket text and logs are available, but duplicate labels for validation may be scarce.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Similarity matching on text and timestamps is established, with some tuning for incident windows.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Flags suggest links; agents can ignore them, so minimal workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Many ITSM tools offer duplicate detection, often as a configurable feature.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Operates on incidents, not people; minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Ticket text and logs may contain user identifiers, so indirect personal data.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that reads commission plan documents and rule tables and converts region- and product-line-specific exceptions into structured, machine-checkable rules that the calculation step can apply consistently.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the pain point that commission rules have many regional and product-line exceptions that are applied inconsistently by hand in spreadsheets. Structuring the rules once reduces per-cycle manual rule lookup, though it still needs human sign-off on every rule.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces inconsistent rule application, but errors in extracted rules would propagate, so the gain depends on review.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports cost control and payroll accuracy, a meaningful but not top-line priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Plan documents exist but are likely in varied formats and may contain ambiguous exception language.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Document parsing with a validation layer, moderate integration effort.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Sales Ops reviews extracted rules, a modest change to their workflow.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Generic document extraction tools exist, but commission-rule structuring needs custom configuration.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Commission rule parsing involves no profiling of workers and no Annex III use, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Plan documents are largely business rules, with only indirect personal data.

use_cases.description: A classifier that checks each commission calculation against the structured rules and the sales transactions, flagging records that are likely to be disputed or contain mismatches (e.g., territory conflicts, unusual exception applications) before payroll submission.
use_cases.justification: Targets the error-prone calculations and the disputes from reps, plus the tight payroll deadline. Pre-flagging likely errors gives the team time to correct them before payroll cut-off rather than after reps complain.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Systematically catches mismatches that manual spreadsheet review misses, improving consistency.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports payroll accuracy and cost control, and reduces dispute handling.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Transaction and territory data is likely structured, but territory assignments may be stale.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Rule-based checks plus simple anomaly flags on structured data, moderate integration with sales systems.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Sales Ops keeps final authority over corrections, a small workflow change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Commission-management platforms cover parts of this, but tailoring to NordIndus rules needs custom work.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Flags calculation records, not an evaluation of worker performance, so minimal risk; should not be used to rank reps for pay or promotion without re-review.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Uses rep identifiers and sales transactions, which are indirectly personal.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that reads onboarding documents submitted through any channel (email attachments, portal uploads, scans) and extracts key fields (name, ID number, right-to-work dates, tax form fields, contract terms) into a structured onboarding record for HR to review.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the pain point that documents arrive through multiple disconnected channels and HR must manually read and re-key each one. Consolidating intake into structured data removes much of the manual handling, though HR still verifies the outputs.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Reduces re-keying errors, but extraction errors on scans still need human checking, so gains are moderate.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports faster start-dates and compliance hygiene, a useful but not top-line priority.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Documents are varied in format and scan quality across channels, so extraction reliability is mixed.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Document AI on standard forms is mature, but integrating several intake channels adds work.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: New hires and HR must use a single intake route, a moderate process change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Mature document-AI services cover ID, tax and contract extraction.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Processes onboarding data without profiling or ranking candidates, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Processes ID numbers, right-to-work and tax data, which are sensitive personal data requiring strict safeguards.

use_cases.description: A checklist assistant that, for each new hire, shows HR which required documents are present, missing, or expired against the compliance checklist, and drafts reminder messages to the new hire for missing items. HR makes every decision.
use_cases.justification: Targets the pain point that HR manually checks each document against the compliance checklist and that missing documents delay system access. A completeness view and automated reminders should shorten the chase cycle. It is a different pain point from extraction, so it does not overlap.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Consistent checklist application reduces missed items, though HR still judges validity.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports compliance and faster productive start, both priorities.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Depends on the checklist being consistently recorded and document status being captured.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Rule-based checklist matching with templated messages is low complexity.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: HR keeps its decisions, and new hires receive reminders, so the change is modest.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: HR onboarding platforms already offer checklist tracking and reminders.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Checks document completeness, not candidate ranking or worker evaluation, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Handles employee identity and employment documents, which are sensitive personal data.

use_cases.description: An AI tool that takes inspectors' free-text notes and site photos and converts them into structured inspection records with standardized hazard categories, severity, location, and required fields, prompting the inspector to complete gaps before submission.
use_cases.justification: Addresses the inconsistent detail in free-text notes by enforcing a consistent structure and capturing the same fields every time, which also makes later cross-site analysis possible.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Standardized fields and gap prompts make records more consistent than free text.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Supports safety compliance, a top priority for an industrial distributor's operations.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Checklists and photos exist, but free-text quality varies and needs cleanup.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Mature LLM or form-extraction tools handle note structuring with modest integration.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Inspectors still submit, but must complete structured fields, a moderate change.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Several inspection and EHS platforms offer AI-assisted structured capture.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Logs hazards on sites, no profiling of workers, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Inspector names and possibly workers in site photos are indirectly personal data.

use_cases.description: A classifier that groups new and historical inspection findings into recurring hazard clusters across sites and flags repeat hazard patterns to the safety team for review.
use_cases.justification: Targets the manual cross-referencing of past reports to find recurring hazards by automating the pattern detection, so the safety team can act on trends across sites.

criteria_rationale.quality_impact: Surfaces repeat hazards consistently that manual review tends to miss across many reports.
criteria_rationale.strategic_alignment: Directly supports injury prevention and compliance priorities.
criteria_rationale.data_quality: Incident history exists but depends on the structured taxonomy from the first use case.
criteria_rationale.technical_complexity: Requires clustering tuned to the company's hazard taxonomy and history.
criteria_rationale.adoption_risk: Safety team reviews flagged patterns, so little change to inspectors' work.
criteria_rationale.off_the_shelf: Generic clustering is common, but tuning to site hazard categories is a custom build.
criteria_rationale.ai_act: Analyses hazards and sites, not individual worker behaviour, so minimal risk.
criteria_rationale.gdpr: Mostly site-level data, with inspector identifiers in records only indirectly personal.
